subject: PrivDeploy acceptance: readiness checkpoints, evidence, and routing fallback plan

Subject: PrivDeploy acceptance: initial evidence and connectivity questions

Diego / team —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. NetOps asked me to collect a short list of items we need to pass your acceptance gate so we can schedule a test cutover. High level asks from our side:

- Confirm required egress IPs (we prefer static egress at the edge)
- Port/protocol list for healthchecks + control plane: currently we see TCP 443 + ephemeral for KV cache sync — please confirm exact ranges
- KMS integration pattern (bring-your-own vs. Redwood-managed) and what evidence you need for key rotation policies
- Any required BGP or private peering configuration (we run a routed overlay)

Attached is our initial traceroute bundle and current firewall policy export. If you can reply with a checklist and a short timeline for evidence review we can line up the network team.

Thanks —
Alex Rivera
Sr. Cloud Engineer, Vanguard Health
ops@vanguardhealth.com

From: diego_fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy acceptance: initial evidence and connectivity questions

Alex — thanks for the packet and the clear list. Below is the minimal acceptance checklist we use for PrivDeploy VPC/on‑prem intake (short form). I included a couple of follow-ups inline.

Required acceptance checkpoints (we'll validate during smoke tests):
1) Static egress IPs or stable NAT mapping (recommended): list the CIDRs you will reserve for test and production. If static egress is not possible, provide a ROI for port-to-IP translation and a NAT mapping table.
2) Allowlist: TCP 443 inbound from your bastion range to the control plane; outbound TCP 443 to our collector endpoints; UDP 53 to Redwood-managed DNS resolvers (unless you provide equivalent).
3) Ports:
   - Control plane: TCP 443 (API, control signals)
   - Model RPCs: TCP 31113 (default, can be mapped)
   - Health and metrics: TCP 9000–9010
   - KV sync: ephemeral TCP 50000–51000 (we can collapse if you have constrained NAT)
4) BGP / peering: optional — if you have private routing we support a routed overlay. Share your ASNs and preferred prefixes (we run iBGP for multi-site).
5) KMS: BYOK supported via customer KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault). We need: key ARN, rotation policy doc, and a test-encrypt/decrypt evidence bundle. If you prefer Redwood-managed keys, confirm customer approval for key escrow.
6) Service accounts & SCP: provide a read-only service account for initial smoke; list IAM roles and the minimum privilege matrix.
7) Audit evidence: SOC2 export (if available), firewall logs for the smoke window, and packet captures for failed healthchecks.

Timeline & next steps:
- Thu 30 Oct: Redwood reviews the evidence you attached and replies with any gaps (we'll stamp green/yellow/red).
- Mon 3 Nov: Dry-run smoke test (15–30 minutes) — requires all allowlists in place.
- Wed 5 Nov: Go/no‑go signoff window.

Questions for Vanguard NetOps (quick):
- Can you provide static egress CIDRs for two test IPs and a production block?
- Are there any mandated maintenance windows between 00:00–06:00 UTC that would prevent a Monday dry-run?

I'll attach a short mutual action plan (spreadsheet) once we confirm the CIDRs. cc'ing Marissa for compliance evidence intake and Ben for ops readiness.

Best —
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198
Diego.fernandez@redwood.ai

Attachments: RDW-privdeploy-checklist-short.pdf

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy acceptance: initial evidence and connectivity questions

Quick confirmations from infra/security:

- We can support TCP 31113 being mapped to an alternate port if Vanguard requires (we usually keep 31113 for model RPCs but will map for constrained environments).
- KV sync ephemeral range: if Vanguard's NAT collapses ephemeral ports, we can configure a static port pool (50020–50040) for KV traffic — please confirm.
- Auditing: Marissa will accept firewall logs in either raw syslog or JSON export; prefer JSON for rapid parsing.

Do you have a preference for KMS rotation cadence? If Vanguard wants 90‑day rotation, we need the rotation schedule in the evidence packet to avoid a late gap.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Alex — great, this is clean and we can proceed on the timeline. Confirmations and next items below (finalized mutual action plan attached).

Finalized checklist (short):
- Static egress: Vanguard will reserve 198.51.100.45/46 for test; production /28 block confirmed. Redwood will use those IPs in allowlists during the dry-run.
- KV sync: we'll use static port pool 50020–50040 for the dry-run to avoid NAT collapse issues. Please open and map accordingly.
- Ports & protocols: accept as listed. Ben will run the smoke orchestration and drop a readout in the channel.
- KMS: Vanguard to provide test key ARN and a signed rotation policy PDF by COB Mon 3 Nov. Marissa will intake compliance docs.
- Evidence: upload firewall logs (JSON) and packet captures to the Confluence page linked below by Mon 3 Nov 12:00 PST.

Doc & signature: I attached RDW-Vanguard-MAP-20251101.xlsx — please review and route to contracts for signature. Contracts can use the DocuSign link below.

Fallback routing note: if the production cutover hits unexpected NAT translation failures, we'll failover to Hosted API for read-only traffic while we remediate. That fallback plan requires an explicit acknowledgement from Vanguard during the go/no‑go window.

Proposed dry-run schedule:
- Mon 3 Nov 14:00 PDT: pre-check (15m)
- Mon 3 Nov 15:00 PDT: smoke (15–30m)
- Tue 4 Nov 10:00 PDT: results and remediation ticket if needed

Please reply with a one-line ack for each bullet above so we can move contracts into signature.

Cheers —
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
